Nowswap, a decentralized exchange on Ethereum, was attacked by a flash loan. The attacker emptied Nowswap’s liquidity pool. The liquidity pool was reduced from US$1,069,197 to US$24.15. The attacker made a profit of 536,000 USDT and 158 WETH. A total of more than 1 million US dollars. The attacker used the K value verification vulnerability in the Nowswap USDT/WETH transaction pair contract to perform multiple exchanges, and each exchange obtained multiple times the normal due assets, until the assets in the trading pair pool were exhausted.

NowSwap, a decentralized exchange on Ethereum, was exploited on 15 September 2021 due to a mismatched arithmetic constant in its AMM contract, enabling an attacker to swap a minimal input for nearly the entire pool. The incident resulted in the theft of over $1.1 million, including 158.29 WETH and 535,706 USDT, which were laundered via Tornado Cash. A critical arithmetic error stemmed from the inconsistent use of a pool constant ('K') after a contract update. One validation still used the old value, permitting attacker swaps that drained almost all pooled assets.
